scope: finite exact microscopes for the two cross-cutting F3 rows
claim_boundary: This closes the registered F3 interaction-law rows at bounded finite scope only. It does not establish G6 capability prediction or empirical universality.

rows.ledger_row: Identify superadditive thresholds where capabilities appear only jointly.
rows.scope: two finite distinction capacities whose jointly usable code space is Cartesian-product sized
assumptions: baseline capacities are a0 and b0 and upgrades yield a1>=a0 and b1>=b0
the obligation requires at least N pairwise distinguishable joint cells
joint distinguishability capacity is exactly a*b
success is the threshold predicate a*b >= N
rows.theorem: A capability appears only jointly exactly when a1*b1 >= N while a1*b0 < N and a0*b1 < N (with the baseline also below N). This gives a strict positive discrete interaction in the success indicator. Witness: a0=b0=1, a1=b1=2, N=4.
rows.strongest_parent: complementarity / threshold production on a Cartesian code space
rows.negative_twin: set N=2 in the witness; either upgrade alone reaches threshold, so the joint-only emergence disappears
rows.nearest_counterexample: if the two capacities are not jointly usable as a Cartesian code, the product law need not hold
rows.falsifier: a parameter tuple satisfying the stated inequalities where joint-only success does not occur, or joint-only success where one inequality fails

rows.ledger_row: Identify interference cases where adding one component harms another.
rows.scope: one capability under a frozen hard resource budget with mandatory maintenance cost for an added component
assumptions: capability A succeeds iff it receives at least Q resource units
A alone may use the full budget
adding component B imposes unavoidable maintenance cost M from the same budget
no compensating benefit from B is counted in A's metric
rows.theorem: Adding B harms A exactly when R >= Q but R-M < Q. If adding B is a free optional extension that preserves the old feasible allocation (M=0 or old allocation remains feasible), optimal A performance cannot decrease; therefore genuine interference requires a load-bearing cost/coupling/constraint that removes an old feasible solution.
rows.negative_twin: raise budget to R+M or make B optional/free; A's previous feasible allocation is restored and the harm vanishes
rows.nearest_counterexample: if B's presence improves A enough to offset its maintenance cost, net A performance may increase despite shared-budget contention
rows.falsifier: a frozen-budget instance satisfying R>=Q and R-M<Q where A remains feasible without an unmetered resource, or a free optional extension that lowers the optimum
